title: When Smart Cities Turn Menacing
gist: Wairagala Wakabi argues Uganda and several other African countries are adopting digital-surveillance tools nominally for safety and counterterrorism but increasingly using them for political control; Uganda's 2025 EPSAuto traffic system is the example. Excerpt only.

themes.theme: Surveillance tech and political control in Africa

insights.claim: Uganda has embraced digital-surveillance tools in the name of improving public safety and combating terrorism, and the pattern is repeating across several African countries.
insights.speaker: WAIRAGALA WAKABI
insights.so_what: Surveillance-tech procurement in Africa carries governance and sanction risk.

insights.claim: African governments are increasingly using smart-city and surveillance technologies for political control rather than national security.
insights.speaker: WAIRAGALA WAKABI
insights.so_what: Political-risk factor for companies selling or financing such systems.

insights.claim: In June 2025 Uganda switched on the Automated Express Penalty System (EPSAuto), using CCTV, automatic number plate recognition and an intelligent transport monitoring system to fine motorists, and it quickly generated controversy.
insights.speaker: WAIRAGALA WAKABI
insights.so_what: Concrete example of dual-use urban surveillance infrastructure being rolled out.
